title: runtime: fetch + cache quantization profiles from model registry
author: Noah Patel
body:
Summary
This PR adds the runtime codepath to resolve quantization profiles by fetching profile artifacts from the model registry, caching them in-process, and invalidating the cache when the referenced profile version changes.

This is the plumbing needed for route-scoped quantization enablement (policy/config comes in a follow-up PR), and unblocks perf/evals to validate the “library” profiles against real runtime execution.

Motivation / context
- Profiles are published/owned by Redwood and stored in the model registry as versioned artifacts.
- The runtime must be able to: (1) resolve a profile ref -> artifact, (2) verify integrity, (3) keep hot paths fast via caching, and (4) stay safe when profiles are updated/rolled back.

Design (high level)
- New runtime component: QuantizationProfileResolver
  - Input: ProfileRef (profile_id + version OR profile_id + channel=latest), ModelId, HardwareInfo (gpu_arch/compute_capability), and a “sequence length regime” hint (short/medium/long; currently derived from request max_tokens + observed prompt length).
  - Output: ResolvedProfile (selected quantization variant + kernel constraints + calibration metadata + resolved manifest digest) or a typed error.
- Model registry integration
  - Fetch profile manifest from model-registry service (internal) and then fetch the referenced artifact blob(s).
  - Verify manifest signature (using existing runtime trust bundle) and validate schema via the already-landed quant profile JSON schema types.
- Caching
  - In-memory cache (per-worker) with LRU + TTL.
  - Cache key: (profile_id, resolved_version, gpu_arch, runtime_abi_version)
    - NOTE: We intentionally do not include tenant/org in key since library profiles are global and immutable once resolved_version is known.
  - Two-level caching:
    1) “Latest pointer” cache: profile_id -> (version, etag, fetched_at)
    2) “Artifact cache”: key above -> ResolvedProfile
  - Negative caching for transient fetch failures is bounded (short TTL) to avoid tight retry loops.
- Invalidation
  - If ProfileRef uses channel=latest, we periodically re-check the latest pointer (ETag + If-None-Match) and refresh when version changes.
  - If ProfileRef pins a version, we treat it as immutable and cache until TTL expiry (still verified on load).
- Failure behavior
  - Failure to fetch/resolve a profile returns “NoProfileResolved” to caller; caller will continue baseline execution (no hard failure).
  - We emit metrics and structured logs on resolution failures.

Implementation details
- Added runtime/quant_profiles/resolver.{cc,h}
  - Performs manifest fetch, signature verify, schema validate, and variant selection for the current hardware.
  - Variant selection logic is intentionally conservative: if multiple variants match, choose the highest-precision variant available for that hardware (bf16/fp16 > int8 > int4). (This is temporary; later PR will incorporate policy preferences.)
- Added runtime/quant_profiles/cache.{cc,h}
  - Thread-safe LRU w/ TTL, sized via config.
  - Avoids duplicate fetches by using a per-key singleflight gate (promise/future) so concurrent requests for the same key coalesce to one fetch.
- Added model-registry client calls (internal)
  - Uses existing runtime HTTP client pool.
  - Supports ETag conditional requests for “latest pointer” reads.
- Observability
  - Metrics:
    - runtime_quant_profile_lookup_total{result=hit|miss|error}
    - runtime_quant_profile_fetch_total{result=success|error, stage=manifest|artifact}
    - runtime_quant_profile_cache_entries
    - runtime_quant_profile_cache_evictions_total
  - Logs include profile_id, resolved_version, gpu_arch, and error_type.

Config
- New runtime config flags (defaults chosen to be safe for beta):
  - quant_profiles.cache.max_entries (default: 256)
  - quant_profiles.cache.ttl_seconds (default: 900)
  - quant_profiles.latest_pointer.ttl_seconds (default: 60)
  - quant_profiles.fetch.timeout_ms (default: 750)

Test plan
- Unit tests:
  - Cache behavior: TTL expiry, LRU eviction, negative-cache TTL.
  - Singleflight behavior: N concurrent resolutions perform exactly 1 fetch.
  - Manifest validation: rejects invalid signature / schema.
- Integration tests (runtime harness):
  - Starts local stub model-registry server; serves manifest + artifact.
  - Verifies invalidation when “latest” points to a new version.
  - Verifies baseline fallback on registry 5xx/timeouts.

Performance considerations
- Cache hit path is lock-minimized (shared lock for read + atomic timestamp refresh).
- Artifact decompression happens once per resolved key and stays cached.
- “Latest pointer” checks are gated by TTL and use conditional requests.

Rollout notes
- This PR only adds the resolver + cache. It is not yet wired to route-level enablement.
- The resolver is behind the existing runtime feature gate quant_profiles.enabled=false by default in prod.

Follow-ups
- Wire resolver into request execution path + compatibility checks/fallback on kernel mismatch (ENG-18451 / PRs upcoming).
- Add richer tagging for traces and downstream cost attribution (telemetry PR).
- Consider adding jitter/backoff if we see registry thundering-herd during fleet deploys (watch during beta).

Commits
1) runtime: add QuantizationProfileResolver interface + wiring
2) runtime: implement LRU+TTL cache and singleflight fetch coalescing
3) runtime: model-registry client for quant profile manifest + artifact blobs
4) tests: cache TTL/LRU + latest-pointer invalidation + stub registry
5) obs: add basic metrics + structured logs for fetch/resolve

Changed areas (high level)
- runtime/quant_profiles/
- runtime/config/
- runtime/metrics/
- runtime/tests/integration/model_registry_stub/

Illustrative snippet
- ETag-based latest pointer refresh:
  - If-None-Match: <etag>
  - 304 => keep cached version
  - 200 => parse new version, invalidate artifact cache entries for (profile_id, old_version, *)

Review conversation (highlights)
- Hiro Tanaka: “Please make the cache key include runtime ABI version so we don’t accidentally reuse artifacts across kernel changes.”
  - Noah Patel: Added runtime_abi_version to cache key + test coverage.
- Quentin Harris: “Use conditional GETs for latest pointer reads; otherwise this will be noisy.”
  - Noah Patel: Implemented ETag + If-None-Match for pointer fetch and added metric for 304 rate.
- Sean Gallagher: “Timeout is too high for the hot path; ensure we fail open and don’t stall requests.”
  - Noah Patel: Reduced default timeout to 750ms, ensured caller receives typed NoProfileResolved and continues baseline; added integration test for timeout.
- Mateo Alvarez: “Singleflight is good; can we cap concurrent in-flight fetches to avoid local saturation?”
  - Noah Patel: Added per-process semaphore (max 32 in-flight profile fetches) with metric for throttled waits.
